sentences.text: Osteolepis was an extinct genus of lobe-finned fish that lived during the Devonian period.
This fish grew to be approximately 20 centimeters long and was covered in large, square scales.
Both the scales and the head plates were protected by a thin layer of spongy bone known as cosmine.
Canals connecting the cosmine layer to sensory cells likely allowed Osteolepis to sense vibrations in the water.
Anoxic events in deep water likely caused mass fish kills that preserved articulated fossils of the animal.
The genus name Osteolepis was first coined in 1829 by Sedgwick and Murchison.
A detailed scientific description of the genus was published in 1835 by the naturalist Louis Agassiz.
The species O. panderi was named in 1948 by the paleontologist Erik Jarvik.
Species O. arenatus, O. microlepidotus, and O. major are now considered synonymous with the type species O. macrolepidotus.
Osteolepis likely fed on small invertebrates like arthropods and mollusks.
The fish was likely prey for larger fish such as Cheirolepis.
As a rhipidistian fish, Osteolepis shared several characteristics with tetrapods.
It was a tetrapodomorph distantly related to tetrapods.
Osteolepis belongs to the family Osteolepididae and the order Osteolepiformes.
Osteolepis lived in Lake Orcadie in northern Scotland.
The animal inhabited the Orcadian lakes of northern Scotland.
Osteolepis lived from the Eifelian to the Famennian stages, between 393.47 and 358.86 million years ago.
Its habitat was a calm freshwater lake that experienced periodic drying.
It is debated whether early distinctions between Osteolepis species were based on real anatomy or taphonomic artifacts.
